mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.1% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.2% signals rising inflation, prompting Fed rate hike expectations that compress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous acceleration in GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above 12-month averages indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 and HOUST both exceed 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment periods (UNRATE > 7.0%), a rising UNRATE signals worsening labor market conditions and recessionary fears, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises in high unemployment periods (UNRATE > 7.0%).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO decline exceeding 0.5% indicates weakening economic output, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days due to reduced earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO falls > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising retail sales figure (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days as economic growth accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are negative in > 60% of instances when RSAFS rises.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline signal labor market strengthening, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days due to improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly FEDFUNDS increase exceeding 0.1% signals monetary tightening, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations to produce negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1%.
